packages.label: חִלּוּל שַׁבָּת וּפְסִיעוֹת קְצָרוֹת
packages.reason: These nodes all share the essential nature of 'departure / withdrawal / diminishment.' Chilul Shabbat is a chalal (hollow, withdrawn space); chalal is histalkut (departure/ascent of the holy); 'ki yimatzeh chalal ba'adamah' is the scriptural expression of that same hollow. Pesi'ot ktzarot (shortened steps) and 'pesi'otav mitkatzarot' are both expressions of the same contraction — the walking diminished, the mitzvah's legs weakened. Shabbat as 'first wife' and its desecration as her death complete the cluster: the death of the first wife IS the shortened step IS chilul Shabbat. All nodes describe the same reality of sacred diminishment / degraded walking.

merge_notes.reason: CC2 (shabbat — first wife) is a 2-node isolated pair. The text explicitly defines Shabbat as 'first wife' (bechina), and the entire discourse on chilul Shabbat hinges on this equation: desecrating Shabbat = 'killing' the first wife = shortened steps. The shared nature is the Shabbat entity itself — שבת and אשתו ראשונה are the same thing from two angles (the holy day and the intimate partner-soul). They belong in the Shabbat cluster with chilul shabbat, chalal, and pesi'ot ktzarot.

packages.label: תָּמָר בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְהַמְתָּקַת הַדִּינִים
packages.label_en: The Date Palm of Holiness and the Sweetening of Judgments
packages.reason: These three nodes share the essential nature of the holy resolution of conflict. 'Tzaddik ka-tamar yifrach' (the righteous one flourishes like a date palm) is the positive outcome of the tzaddik's machloket — it IS the sweetening of the judgments. Tamar bi-kedushah is the abstract concept; 'tzaddik ka-tamar yifrach' is its scriptural expression; ha-matak ha-dinim is its functional identity. The three are different faces of the same reality: holy flourishing that nullifies the evil tamar (sitra achra).

packages.label: סִּטְרָא אָחֳרָא וְתָּמָר הָרָע
packages.label_en: The Sitra Achra and the Evil Tomar
packages.reason: These nodes all share the essential nature of the evil force — the realm of din, opposition, and inversion. The sitra achra IS machloket (conflict/dispute is the very substance of the evil side). The tomar of the sitra achra IS the shaor (leaven = concentrated din = Elohim squared and filled = the evil 'tamar' which means temura/inversion). Eretz Canaan IS 'kan ani' (here is poverty) — the condition that arises from machloket, which is the sitra achra. Canaan as poverty is a bechina of the same evil domain: conflict strips prosperity, the sitra achra's expression in the earthly realm. All nodes name the same essential force: the evil power of machloket/din/sitra achra in its various faces.

merge_notes.reason: CC7 is a 2-node pair: tomar of the sitra achra = shaor ba-kachovet (leaven in the date). The text defines the tomar of sitra achra as 'temura' (inversion) — it is the anti-tamar, the inversion of wisdom = foolishness, inversion of life = death. Shaor is 'klalut ve-tokef ha-dinim,' the concentrated force of harsh judgment. Both are names for the same evil entity. They share the essential nature of the sitra achra's concentrated din-force. This belongs with the sitra achra / machloket cluster as the same domain of evil.

CC5 is a 3-node cluster: eretz Canaan = Canaan = 'here is poverty.' The text says when machloket exists, the land is called Canaan. Canaan IS 'kan ani' (poverty). This is not a cause-effect relationship — the poverty IS the Canaan nature, which IS the expression of machloket in the material world. Canaan as poverty-land is a bechina of the same evil domain as machloket/sitra achra. The sitra achra's grip creates the Canaan condition. The essential shared nature is: the evil force as it manifests in depletion of resources and spiritual poverty.

packages.label: שָׁלוֹם וְהָרְפוּאוֹת
packages.reason: These three nodes share the essential nature of wholeness, integration, and the healing power that flows when conflict is absent. Shalom IS 'eretz natna yevulah' (the land gives its produce) — when peace reigns, the earth is fully generative. Refu'ot (medicines/healings) ARE shalom — the healing force is a bechina of peace itself, not merely produced by it. The Rebbe explicitly states 'ha-refu'ot she-hem bechina shalom.' All three express the single quality of integrated wholeness that is the opposite of machloket.
